items.issue: No null/undefined guard on wallet parameter.
items.evidence: Calling classifyPatterns(null) throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'trades'). Same for undefined.
items.impact: If route.ts constructs malformed WalletData or a bug passes null, the entire analyze endpoint crashes with an unhandled 500.
items.fix: Add `if (!wallet || !wallet.trades) return { walletAddress: wallet?.address ?? 'unknown', chain: wallet?.chain ?? 'unknown', amplify: [], guard: [] };`

items.issue: If wallet.trades is undefined or null, .filter() throws. wallet.approvals same risk at line 171.
items.evidence: `const profitableSells = trades.filter(...)` where trades=undefined → TypeError.
items.impact: Server 500 if cached/demo data has missing trades array.
items.fix: Guard at function entry (see 18.1.1).

items.issue: No null guard on `result` parameter. If result is null/undefined, `result.amplify` throws TypeError. If label is null/undefined, persona.walletLabel becomes null/undefined. If pnlTotal is NaN, it propagates silently.
items.evidence: In route.ts:66: `generatePersona(p, walletResults[i].chain === 'solana' ? 'SOLANA SELF' : 'ETHEREUM SELF', walletResults[i].realizedPnl)`. `walletResults[i].realizedPnl` comes from `parseFloat(overview.realizedPnlUsd) || 0` which guards NaN via `|| 0`, but TypeScript allows NaN through.
items.impact: If classifyPatterns returns a malformed result or route.ts passes a bad index, persona generation crashes. NaN pnlTotal silently renders as NaN in UI.
items.fix: Add `if (!result) return defaultPersona(label ?? 'Unknown', 0);`. Use `Number.isFinite(pnlTotal) ? pnlTotal : 0`.

items.issue: If either parameter is NaN, gap = NaN, and all comparisons (NaN > 20, NaN > 10) are false, silently returning the 'professional level' message — misleading.
items.evidence: `const gap = topWinRate - userWinRate;` — with NaN inputs: `NaN - NaN = NaN`, `NaN > 20` → false, `NaN > 10` → false. Falls through to default 'professional level' string.
items.impact: Misleading UX: user with corrupted data sees 'You're trading at a professional level'.
items.fix: Add `if (!Number.isFinite(userWinRate) || !Number.isFinite(topWinRate)) return 'Unable to compare — data unavailable.';`

items.issue: If parent renders WalletInput without onSubmit prop, `onSubmit(parsed)` throws TypeError. No defensive check.
items.evidence: `onSubmit(parsed)` at line 33 — no `if (!onSubmit) return;` or `onSubmit?.()` guard.
items.impact: Component crash if used incorrectly. Unlikely in current app (always passed) but violates defensive coding.
items.fix: Use optional chaining: `onSubmit?.(parsed)` or guard at function top.

items.issue: If request body is {} or {addresses: null}, `for (const addr of body.addresses)` throws TypeError: undefined/null is not iterable.
items.evidence: `const body: AnalyzeRequest = await req.json();` then `for (const addr of body.addresses)` — no `if (!Array.isArray(body.addresses))` guard.
items.impact: Any malformed POST body (e.g. {}) returns 500 instead of 400 Bad Request.
items.fix: Add `if (!Array.isArray(body?.addresses)) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'addresses array required' }, { status: 400 });`

items.pattern: AMP-06 — Math.min() edge case with no losing trades
items.issue: `Math.min(...trades.filter((t) => t.pnlPct < 0).map((t) => t.pnlPct), 0)` — the trailing `,0` guards the empty-array case. However, if ALL trades have pnlPct of exactly 0, none pass the `< 0` filter, so maxLoss becomes 0 and `Math.abs(0) <= 20` is true. AMP-06 fires with maxLoss of 0 even though there were no actual drawdowns to measure.
items.evidence: Line 104: `const maxLoss = Math.min(...trades.filter((t) => t.pnlPct < 0).map((t) => t.pnlPct), 0);` then line 105: `if (Math.abs(maxLoss) <= 20)`. With no losing trades, maxLoss=0, condition=true.
items.impact: Minor logic quirk: a wallet with 5+ profitable buys and zero sells gets 'Consistent Compound' with max drawdown 0%. True but not meaningful.
items.fix: Consider requiring at least one losing trade: `const losingPcts = trades.filter(t => t.pnlPct < 0).map(t => t.pnlPct); if (losingPcts.length > 0) { const maxLoss = Math.min(...losingPcts); ... }`

items.pattern: AMP-02 — stop-loss boundary value pnlPct exactly -15
items.issue: `t.pnlPct > -15` uses strict inequality. A trade that lost exactly -15.0% is excluded from the 'disciplined defender' stop-loss band. The boundary -15 is excluded.
items.evidence: Line 42: `t.pnlPct < 0 && t.pnlPct > -15`. Value -15.0 fails `> -15`.
items.impact: Design decision: is -15% a stop-loss or too deep? No documented rationale. Minor inconsistency risk.
items.fix: Document boundary rationale or use `>=` if -15 is an acceptable stop-loss threshold.

items.issue: `t.holdDurationDays > 30` excludes exactly-30-day holds. Same pattern at AMP-03 (`< 1` excludes 1-day), AMP-05 (`> 14` excludes 14-day), GRD-01 (`> 7` excludes 7-day). All strict — no documented rationale.
items.evidence: Lines 25, 56, 88, 128: strict inequalities throughout.
items.impact: Trades exactly at threshold values are silently excluded from patterns. Likely intentional but undocumented.
items.fix: Document threshold rationale in comments.

items.issue: `t.holdDurationDays < 1` matches duration of 0 and negative values. Zero-duration trades (same-block buy+sell?) qualify as 'meme entries'. Negative durations (data errors) also match.
items.evidence: Line 56: `t.holdDurationDays < 1`. 0 < 1 → true. -5 < 1 → true.
items.impact: Data errors (negative hold durations) could inflate meme-sniper detection. Zero-duration trades may not be true memes.
items.fix: Use `t.holdDurationDays > 0 && t.holdDurationDays < 1` to exclude zero/negative.

items.issue: `t.holdDurationDays * 24 < 3` matches 0 and negative values. For negative, `-1 * 24 = -24`, which is < 3.
items.evidence: Line 73: same pattern as 18.2.4.
items.impact: Same data-quality risk as 18.2.4.
items.fix: Add `t.holdDurationDays > 0 &&` guard.

items.pattern: generateCompareInsight — NaN winRate returns misleading default
items.issue: If userWinRate or topWinRate is NaN, gap = NaN, and NaN comparisons are always false, returning 'professional level' message.
items.evidence: Same analysis as 18.1.4. Also: if userWinRate is MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and topWinRate is 0, gap = -MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, returning 'professional level' — a degenerate comparison.
items.impact: Silently misleading UX when data is corrupted.
items.fix: Guard with Number.isFinite() checks on both inputs.

items.issue: `wallet.avgGasGwei > wallet.networkMedianGasGwei * 2`. If networkMedianGasGwei is 0, condition is `avgGasGwei > 0`. If negative, e.g. -10, condition is `avgGasGwei > -20` — almost always true for non-negative gas. Also: if avgGasGwei is NaN, `NaN > ...` is false, GRD-03 never fires.
items.evidence: Line 158. Solana wallet data at route.ts:79 sets networkMedianGasGwei: 0.
items.impact: Solana wallets: GRD-03 fires on any avgGasGwei > 0 (trivially true for active wallets). This may produce false-positive 'Gas Guzzler' tags on Solana.
items.fix: Guard: `if (wallet.networkMedianGasGwei <= 0) return;` or use chain-appropriate gas medians.

items.issue: `t.amountUsd < 1000` classifies as micro-cap. Trades of exactly 0.00 amountUsd qualify. Negative amountUsd (refunds?) also qualify. No lower bound.
items.evidence: Line 186: `const microCapTotal = trades.filter((t) => t.amountUsd < 1000);`
items.impact: Zero-amount or negative-amount trades skew the micro-cap ratio.
items.fix: Add `t.amountUsd > 0 &&` guard.

items.issue: If pnlPct is Infinity or MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, all `> 0` / `< 0` comparisons work correctly. But `Math.min(...)` with Infinity works (Infinity is the largest number), so `Math.min(Infinity, 0)` = 0. And `Math.abs(Infinity)` = Infinity, `Infinity <= 20` = false. Mostly safe but unvalidated.
items.evidence: No input validation anywhere on numeric trade fields. OnchainOS returns strings — parseFloat could produce Infinity for extremely large string values.
items.impact: Low risk: parseFloat('1e1000') = Infinity. Could cause strange pattern results.
items.fix: Clamp or validate trade numeric fields after parsing.

items.pattern: Regex parsing — no address format validation
items.issue: The regex `/^(\S+)\s*(.*)$/` only checks for non-whitespace characters. It accepts ANY non-whitespace string as an 'address': emoji, null bytes, SQL injection payloads, 10K-character strings, JavaScript code, etc.
items.evidence: Line 18: `const addrMatch = line.match(/^(\S+)\s*(.*)$/);`. `\S` matches any non-whitespace char including `\0`, emoji, `<>"'&|;`, etc. No length limit, no hex/base58 check, no checksum validation.
items.impact: Garbage addresses are sent to OnchainOS API calls (getAllBalances, getPortfolioOverview) which may error or behave unexpectedly. Null bytes could cause issues in systems expecting C strings.
items.fix: Add format validation: Ethereum addresses match `/^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$/`. Solana addresses match `/^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$/`. Reject or sanitize everything else.

items.issue: Empty textarea: `addresses.split('\n').filter(Boolean)` returns `[]`, then `parsed.length === 0` triggers error. Correctly handled.
items.evidence: Line 15: `.filter(Boolean)` removes empty lines. Line 30: `if (parsed.length === 0)` check.
items.impact: No issue — handled.
items.fix: None needed.

items.issue: JS regex `\S` matches null byte (`\0`) as non-whitespace. A line like `\0x123...` would parse address as the string containing `\0`.
items.impact: Null bytes passed to API calls could cause truncation or injection in downstream systems.
items.fix: Filter out null bytes: `addr.replace(/\0/g, '')` before use.

items.issue: `\S+` greedily matches arbitrarily long non-whitespace strings. A single 10,000-character 'address' passes through with no length check.
items.evidence: Line 18: no `addr.length > 100` or similar guard.
items.impact: Giant strings sent as API parameters. Could cause URL length limits, memory pressure, or DoS.
items.fix: Enforce max length: `if (addr.length > 100) { setError(...); return; }`

items.issue: Emoji characters are non-whitespace, so `\S+` matches them. A line of `🚀🌕💎` would be parsed as address `🚀🌕💎`.
items.evidence: JS: `'🚀🌕💎'.match(/^(\S+)\s*(.*)$/)` → matches, capturing `🚀🌕💎`.
items.impact: Emoji 'addresses' passed to OnchainOS would almost certainly error, but the error handling just returns 500.
items.fix: Address format validation (see 18.3.1) inherently rejects emoji.

items.issue: `chainStr.replace(/[()]/g, '').split(/,\s*/).filter(Boolean)` strips parentheses and splits on commas. No validation that resulting chain names are valid chain identifiers.
items.evidence: Line 22. User could enter '0x...abc FOO, BAR, BAZ' and chains would be ['FOO', 'BAR', 'BAZ'].
items.impact: Invalid chain names passed to route.ts. In route.ts line 32: `addr.chains.filter((c) => c !== 'solana')` implicitly treats unknown chains as EVM chains, sending invalid chain parameters to OnchainOS.
items.fix: Whitelist valid chain names: only accept 'ethereum', 'solana', 'xlayer', 'base', etc.

items.issue: `process.env.DEMO_MODE === 'true'` is case-sensitive. `True`, `TRUE`, or `1` would not match.
items.evidence: Line 17: strict equality against literal `'true'`.
items.impact: Minor: deployment misconfiguration could silently disable demo mode.
items.fix: Use case-insensitive: `process.env.DEMO_MODE?.toLowerCase() === 'true'`.

items.issue: `if (parsed.length > 5) { setError('Maximum 5 wallets for the demo.'); return; }` — enforced only in WalletInput component. No corresponding check in the server route.
items.evidence: WalletInput.tsx:31 client-side guard. route.ts:30: `for (const addr of body.addresses)` iterates ALL addresses with no length check.
items.impact: Attacker can bypass the client-side limit by POSTing directly to /api/analyze with 10K addresses, causing server resource exhaustion (10K sequential API calls).
items.fix: Add server-side guard: `if (body.addresses.length > 5) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Maximum 5 wallets' }, { status: 400 });`

items.pattern: Empty addresses array — no guard but works
items.issue: `body.addresses = []` → `for...of` iterates 0 times → `walletResults = []` → `allPatterns = []` → `personas = []` → response has `wallets: 0`, `patterns: []`, `personas: []`. No error thrown.
items.evidence: Tested logically: empty array just produces empty results. No error.
items.impact: Client returns 200 with empty data. Harmless but should arguably be a 400.
items.fix: Return 400 for empty addresses: `if (body.addresses.length === 0) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'At least one wallet address required' }, { status: 400 });`

items.issue: If the same address is submitted multiple times (same or different chain), it's processed multiple times. Each iteration makes identical API calls.
items.evidence: route.ts:30-85: `for (const addr of body.addresses)` iterates every entry. No Set-based dedup on address+chain pairs.
items.impact: Wasted API calls, inflated wallet count, duplicate PatternResults in response.
items.fix: Deduplicate: `const unique = new Map(); for (const a of body.addresses) unique.set(a.address + ':' + a.chains.join(','), a);`

items.pattern: 10K addresses — no rate limiting, sequential processing
items.issue: The `for...of` loop processes addresses sequentially with await-style blocking API calls. 10K addresses would make 20K+ sequential API calls with no timeout, no batching, no rate limiting.
items.evidence: route.ts:30-85: sequential for-of loop with blocking calls to `getAllBalances`, `getPortfolioOverview`, `getApprovals`, `scanTokens` per address.
items.impact: Server hangs for minutes/hours. Next.js API route timeout may kill it before completion. Denial of service vector.
items.fix: Add server-side max-addresses guard (see 18.4.1). Add per-request timeout. Consider Promise.all with concurrency limit for legitimate multi-wallet requests.

items.pattern: Empty trades array — all patterns gracefully produce empty results
items.issue: When `wallet.trades = []`, all `.filter()` calls return `[]`, all `.length >= N` checks fail, no patterns detected. Classifier returns `{ amplify: [], guard: [] }`. Handled correctly.
items.evidence: classifier.ts — every check begins with `.filter()` on trades array, and length guards prevent empty-array issues.
items.impact: No issue — handled.
items.fix: None needed.

items.pattern: Empty approvals array — GRD-04 not triggered
items.issue: `wallet.approvals.filter(...)` on empty array returns `[]`, `length > 5` is false. Correct behavior.
items.evidence: Line 171-172: filter on potentially empty array, then length check.
items.impact: No issue.
items.fix: None needed.

items.issue: `handleAnalyze` sets `setLoading(true)` then immediately calls `fetch`. In React 18 with automatic batching, state updates are batched but the re-render is still asynchronous. Two rapid clicks before the DOM updates the button's `disabled` attribute could fire `handleAnalyze` twice. There is no `useRef`-based guard (e.g., `const running = useRef(false)`) to prevent re-entrancy.
items.evidence: page.tsx:27-37: `const handleAnalyze = async (addresses) => { setLoading(true); ... try { const res = await fetch(...); ... } finally { setLoading(false); } };`. No `if (running.current) return; running.current = true;` pattern.
items.impact: Two concurrent analyze requests: double API calls, interleaved phase transitions from competing timer sets (see 18.5.2). Corrupted UI state.
items.fix: Add `const analyzing = useRef(false);` and guard: `if (analyzing.current) return; analyzing.current = true;` at function start. Reset in finally: `analyzing.current = false;`.

items.pattern: Timer overwrite — old timers NOT cleared on re-invocation (P02 issue)
items.issue: `phaseTimers.current = [t1, t2, t3, t4];` (line 37) overwrites the ref without first calling `clearTimeout` on any previously stored timers. If `handleAnalyze` is called while a prior flow's timers are still pending (20s, 58s, 76s timeouts), the old timers continue to fire and call `setPhase(...)`, `fetch(...)`, etc., colliding with the new flow.
items.evidence: page.tsx:37: `phaseTimers.current = [t1, t2, t3, t4];` — no `phaseTimers.current.forEach(clearTimeout)` before reassignment. Cleanup in useEffect (line 25) only runs on component unmount, not between analyze calls.
items.impact: If user clicks ANALYZE at t=0 and again at t=15s: first flow's t2 fires at t=20s setting phase='battle', but second flow is in phase='scanning' or 'results'. State collisions. First flow's fetch('.api/roast') response arrives and overwrites battleData. First flow's t3 at t=58s overwrites phase again.
items.fix: At start of handleAnalyze, clear existing timers: `phaseTimers.current.forEach(clearTimeout); phaseTimers.current = [];`. This is exactly the fix identified in P02.

items.pattern: Stale closure over phase in setTimeout callbacks
items.issue: The setTimeout callbacks at lines 34-36 capture `setPhase` and `setBattleData`/`setCompareData` via closure. If a new analyze flow starts while old timers are running, the old callbacks still reference the latest state setters (React guarantees setState functions are stable). So the old timers WILL call setPhase('battle')/etc. on the NEW flow's state.
items.evidence: React useState setters are referentially stable across renders. Old timeout closures use the same setPhase function, so they mutate the current render's state.
items.impact: Confirmed: old timer callbacks will corrupt current flow's phase. Combined with 18.5.2, this makes double-click a guaranteed state corruption.
items.fix: Same fix as 18.5.2: clear old timers before starting new flow.

items.pattern: In-flight fetch not aborted on re-invocation
items.issue: If handleAnalyze is called twice, the first `fetch('/api/analyze', ...)` continues in the background. Its response arrives later and `setData(json)` overwrites the second flow's data. No AbortController.
items.evidence: page.tsx:30: `const res = await fetch('/api/analyze', ...)`. No AbortController tied to component lifecycle or a per-request token.
items.impact: First response (stale) overwrites second response data if it arrives after the second completes.
items.fix: Use AbortController: `const ac = new AbortController();` store in ref, abort previous on new call. Add `signal: ac.signal` to fetch.

items.issue: `launchDemo` directly calls `handle(parsed)` with hardcoded addresses. It doesn't go through WalletInput's validation. If `launchDemo` were modified to pass >5 addresses, the client-side limit would be bypassed.
items.evidence: page.tsx:15-16: `const launchDemo = (handle) => handle([{...}, {...}]);`. Only 2 addresses hardcoded — low immediate risk.
items.impact: Low risk currently (hardcoded to 2 addresses). But pattern is fragile — any change to launchDemo could introduce bypass.
items.fix: Move max-address validation into handleAnalyze rather than relying solely on WalletInput.

critical_issue_ids: 18.1.6 — analyze route crashes on missing addresses array
18.5.1 — Double ANALYZE click possible (no ref guard)
18.5.2 — Timer overwrite: old timers not cleared (P02 regression)
top_recommendations: Add null guards to classifyPatterns, generatePersona, and generateCompareInsight
Validate body.addresses is an array in route.ts; return 400 not 500
Add useRef running guard to prevent double-click in handleAnalyze
Clear phaseTimers.current before reassigning (fixes P02 timer overwrite)
Add AbortController for in-flight fetch cancellation on re-invocation
Add address format validation (regex + length + null-byte filter) in WalletInput
Add chain name whitelist validation in WalletInput parsing
Guard GRD-03 against networkMedianGasGwei ≤ 0 (Solana false positives)
Filter zero/negative holdDurationDays in AMP-03 and AMP-04
